proposals.expected_failure_mode: If hospitalization dynamics are not well-approximated by a fixed lag from I (e.g., variable delay or changing severity), delayed_I may mis-time peaks and bias amplitude.
proposals.rationale: Matches prior discovery patterns and surveillance note that admissions can lag the infectious proxy; SEIRS allows waning immunity across the training window while remaining parsimonious for a single age-group weekly series.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Over-delaying can shift peaks too far right, degrading short-horizon forecasts and producing phase error during rapid rise/decline.
proposals.rationale: Alternative plausible lag consistent with surveillance semantics; can better align peak timing if admissions are systematically later than the I proxy in this age group.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H compartment may be weakly identifiable with 31 training weeks, leading to unstable separation of I vs H and overfitting of timing/scale.
proposals.rationale: Directly maps the target (hospitalization rate) to an explicit hospitalization compartment, aligning with recommended observation maps while keeping the observation model simple (no delay).

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the reported series corresponds strictly to incident admissions rather than a combined burden proxy, I+H can inflate levels and distort peak width.
proposals.rationale: Uses combined burden (infectious plus hospitalized) as the observed proxy, which can be more robust when H alone is noisy/weakly identified yet admissions reflect both current infections and ongoing hospital census-like dynamics.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If reinfection/waning materially affects late-season dynamics, SEIR may under-represent tail behavior and mis-estimate decline or secondary bumps.
proposals.rationale: More parsimonious alternative to SEIRS when waning immunity is negligible over the modeled window; retains the key lagged-observation mechanism suggested by surveillance semantics.
